tasks.task:
# Make the DAG Observatory's conversation and timeline tell the truth

## What

Design the decomposition for repairing what the DAG Observatory shows an operator
about a dispatched node: the conversation transcript, the token/cost accounting, the
per-event glyphs and their hover reading, and the timeline lanes. Answer with one
node per subtask, each naming its id, its persona, its dependencies, its `repo` and
`execution_checkout` where it is a lifecycle node, and its task.

The work spans four repositories and a release chain, and deciding how it is cut and
ordered across them is the whole of this dispatch. Nothing below is a node
breakdown — it is measured evidence, gathered so you do not have to re-derive it.

## Why

The operator's own words, verbatim, reading the view against a real run:

> Something's not working quite right with the conversation part of the DAG UI. It
> seems like for some reason it thinks the label is the user messages, and for some
> reason it's not capturing any of the Assistant textual responses, only the tool
> calls. It's also not showing the output for any of the tool calls. And it says no
> assistant text was captured for this run. It doesn't report the input and output
> tokens, the cache, the cost, anything there. I also thought we added specific icons
> for each of the event types, but I'm still seeing only the Marker icon for every
> event. It's weird also that the PR author is showing as running the whole time,
> also a publication track. I also don't know why we would show that the worker is
> still working during publication. It seems like it should be one or the other. We
> also need to have tooltips for event types so that when you hover over an event
> icon, it gives you the details of that event.

This view is how a manager supervises hours of dispatched work they cannot watch
directly. A transcript that shows a persona name where the prompt should be, no
assistant prose, tool calls with no results, and no cost is not a weak view — it is
a view that cannot answer the question it exists for, so the operator falls back to
reading journals by hand. The cost line matters on its own: a single measured turn
in the run below spent $31.22, and the view reports "Not reported".

## Acceptance criteria

- The plan names every subtask, its id, its persona, its dependencies, the
  repository it lands in, and the contract between it and the subtasks consuming it.
- Every one of the seven measured findings below is delivered by some node, or is
  explicitly and reasonedly declined in the plan.
- The wire contract for anything added to a producer is stated with field names and
  types — what a normalized assistant-text event is, what a tool result carries,
  what bounds each is subject to, and what an absent one answers.
- The plan states the order the pieces land in across repositories, and where a
  downstream repository must adopt an upstream release before its own change can be
  proven. Waiting on a release here is a read, not a `kind: human` node: releases on
  this host are automated by release-plz.
- Each node's acceptance criteria are satisfiable by that worker inside its own
  dispatch, and demand that repository's own complete gate where the node changes
  code.
- Every choice this brief left open is either decided in the plan, with the reason,
  or asked of the manager before the plan is finished. Bounding tool-result and
  assistant-text size is one such choice and is explicitly not decided here.

## Additional info

### The repositories, and how a fix travels between them

Four are in play. None of them is built in `ai-orchestrator`, so a subtask against
any of them is a lifecycle node carrying that repository's `repo`:

- `github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness` — normalizes each harness's transcript into
  `ActionEvent`s.
- `github.com/nickderobertis/oneagentgraph` — runs a member's turn and publishes
  `turn-started` / `turn-activity` / `turn-completed` journal events.
- `github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline` — the engine; assembles the conversation
  the read API serves, and links `oneagentgraph`, `onevcs`, and `oneharness` as Rust
  libraries.
- `github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui` — the read API (`onepipeline-api`) and
  the browser bundle (`onepipeline-ui`), both consumed here as published artifacts.

A subtask against `ai-orchestrator` is a lifecycle node too, and this repository's
self-dispatch rule applies: set `execution_checkout: ai-orchestrator-isolated` and
keep `ai-orchestrator` as the publication `repo`.

**The adoption trap, which decides the ordering.** For anything `onepipeline` links,
the version in force in a dispatch is what `onepipeline`'s own `Cargo.lock` resolves
— not the version pinned in `ai-orchestrator/config/`. This has already bitten twice
here: `config/oneagentgraph.version` read 0.3.3 while onepipeline v0.8.1's lock
resolved oneagentgraph 0.3.0, and a real run under it emitted nothing. So a fix
landed in `oneagentgraph` reaches a dispatched worker only once `onepipeline` moves
its lock and releases, and `ai-orchestrator` moves `config/onepipeline.version`.
Widening a `Cargo.toml` caret requirement is a lever connected to nothing; the lock
is the fix. Plan the chain accordingly.

### The seven findings, as measured today

Measured on 2026-08-20 against `runs/issue-27` in the canonical `ai-orchestrator`
checkout, with the read API served by `just telemetry-server` at
`127.0.0.1:8765` and the bundle by `just dag-ui`. Treat each as a starting point to
confirm, not as a conclusion to implement blind — several may share one cause.

**1. The persona name is served as the user message.** `GET
/api/v2/runs/issue-27/conversations/node-scope-1787243453253-993992.worker` answers
`"user": "engineer"` on every turn — `engineer` is the dispatch's `persona` label,
carried on every journal event as `labels.persona`. That is the `YOU / engineer`
bubble the operator sees where the simulated user's prompt should be. Whether the
real prompt is recoverable from the journal at all is part of what to research.

**2. Tool results are dropped at the source.** `oneagentgraph`'s
`src/harness.rs::ingest` returns early for any `ActionEvent` whose `name` is `None`,
and its own doc comment states that a `tool_result` carries no name. `src/judge.rs`
applies the same rule. Its `TurnActivity` payload struct
(`src/event.rs`) has fields `kind`, `name`, `detail`, `truncated` and no `output`
field at all, so a result has nowhere to go even if it were not dropped.
`oneharness`'s `ActionEvent` (`crates/oneharness-core/src/domain/events.rs`) *does*
carry an `output: Option<String>`, so the observation exists upstream and is
discarded. Every `turn-activity` in the journal is `"kind": "tool_call"`; none is a
result.

**3. Assistant prose is normalized nowhere.** `oneharness`'s `ActionEvent` documents
exactly two kinds — `tool_call` and `tool_result`. Claude Code's `stream-json`
`text` content blocks are not mapped to any event, so the assistant's own words are
not in the stream `oneagentgraph` reads. This is the one finding whose fix plausibly
has to start in `oneharness` rather than `oneagentgraph`; confirm that before
assuming it. `ActionEvent.kind` is deliberately a `String` and not an enum,
documented as left open so a new kind never breaks the field.

**4. Usage is in the journal and null in the API.** A real `turn-completed` in
`runs/issue-27/events.jsonl` carries
`{"usage": {"input_tokens": 257955, "output_tokens": 175156, "cache_read_tokens": 45478609, "cache_write_tokens": 423124, "cost_usd": 31.220570500000004}}`.
The read API answers that same turn as
`{"inputTokens": null, "outputTokens": null, "cacheReadTokens": null, "cacheWriteTokens": null, "costUsd": null}`,
and turns that are not `turn-completed` answer `{}` outright. Note that
`oneagentgraph` main's `Usage` struct declares `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`,
`cache_read`, `cache_write`, `cost`, `duration` — a different spelling from the one
in the journal, under `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Establish which producer
version wrote that record and which spelling each side of the seam expects; a
rename that fixes today's runs while breaking the ones already on disk is not a fix.

**5. Turn boundaries collapse.** One worker conversation is served as a single turn
holding 154 tool calls with status `turn-started`; another is three turns where 201
calls sit under one of them. `model` and `durationMs` are null on every turn served.
The journal for that run holds 48 `turn-started` against 11 `turn-completed`, so
part of this is genuine and part is assembly.

**6. Timeline lanes overlap where the work is sequential.** The PR-author and
publication lanes are drawn spanning the whole node, and the worker lane is drawn
active concurrently with publication. The operator's reading is that a worker and
its publication are sequential and should not both be shown running. Decide from the
span data whether the lanes are wrong, the spans are wrong, or the drawing of an
unclosed span is wrong, and say which.

**7. Event markers have no hover reading.** The markers are buttons carrying the
record's name and a category glyph
(`apps/dag-ui/src/features/timeline/event-category.tsx`), with no tooltip. The
existing `TimelinePopover` in that directory serves lane *segments* and documents
why it portals out of the plot's `overflow-hidden` box — the same constraint applies
to a marker tooltip, so read it before designing one.

### One finding is already resolved, and its cause is not

The operator's report that every event draws the same marker glyph was a stale
install, not a missing feature. Per-event-type glyphs shipped in `onepipeline-ui`
0.5.0 (PR #24). `package.json` and `bun.lock` pin 0.5.0, but
`node_modules/onepipeline-ui` held **0.3.3**, because
`ai-orchestrator/scripts/workspace-install.sh` exits 0 having done nothing whenever
`node_modules/.bin/nx` exists — it never reconciles the installed tree against the
lockfile. A pin that moves is therefore invisible to every already-provisioned
checkout until somebody runs `--force`. The manager has already run `--force` in the
canonical checkout, so the served bundle is 0.5.0 now and the glyphs are there.

**The staleness itself is unfixed and is in scope.** It silently serves an old
bundle under a current pin, which is what made six of the seven findings above look
like defects in code that had already moved. Whatever the fix is — reconciling
against the lockfile, or something cheaper that is still honest — it belongs in this
plan as an `ai-orchestrator` node, and this repository's suite drives real recipes
and real Nx, so it is provable end to end in `tests/e2e/`.

### Constraints

- Do not weaken any existing bound to carry new data. `oneagentgraph` bounds
  `TurnActivity.detail` to `MAX_ACTIVITY_DETAIL_CHARS` and flags `truncated`
  deliberately; tool results and assistant prose are both unbounded in the wild and
  need their own answer, which is a decision to bring to the manager rather than to
  take silently.
- The read API's response is a published contract at
  `telemetry_schema_version: 13`, consumed by the shipped browser bundle and by
  anything else reading it. Version or extend it deliberately; do not break it
  incidentally.
- Every repository is verified by its own `just gate` and publishes under its own
  registered rules. Do not plan a change that has to reach a base branch any other
  way.
- Do not plan any node that touches, stops, retries, or writes to a live run. The
  `issue-27` run named above belongs to another manager's session and is evidence to
  read, never to act on. Read-only views and journal reads are fine.
- Accuracy first. A node that repairs the wire contract honestly and lands slower is
  preferred over one that makes the view look right by inventing data the producer
  never captured — "No assistant text was captured for this run" is the correct
  answer whenever no assistant text was in fact captured, and it must stay correct.
